Absolutely loved the fact that it's not trying to please anybody and give people an authentic experience. The sambar and chutney were exactly what is made at home.

The packaging was refreshingly good. The dosa came in a pizza type box which kept the shape intact and the idlis were in a nice plate box. Loved everything about this.

The manager was sweet enough to call up and tell us the taste we'd expect from the sambar would be different from what we're used to eating but tbh, that's exactly what we wanted.

I think I've found a permanent breakfast place in Mumbai! Can't wait for them to start making vadas too. 100% recommend this place if you want a authentic experience. You'll find the mainstream kinds everywhere, this was uniquely "homely". Love it!

featured_reviews.name: Prashant “Paddy” Demello
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re a seafood lover in Mumbai and haven’t eaten at Nityananda Lunch Home in Goregaon East, you’re seriously missing out. Tucked away on a busy stretch, this humble joint has earned a legendary reputation among locals for serving affordable, flavorful, and authentic coastal cuisine. What makes Nityananda truly special is its inclusiveness — you’ll see everyone from daily wage workers to white-collar professionals eating side by side, enjoying the same spicy, satisfying food.

The restaurant specializes in Malvani, Konkani, and South Indian seafood, and the flavors are as real as it gets. Their seafood curries — especially the prawns curry, bangda curry, surmai gravy, and fish thalis — are packed with the kind of rustic, homestyle masalas that make you want to lick your fingers. The curries tend to be on the oilier side, but that’s part of the charm — it gives the dishes a rich, bold taste that’s hard to find in high-end restaurants.

I personally love their South Indian seafood curries — the balance of coconut, curry leaves, and tamarind is spot on. The fish is always fresh, and the portions are generous for the price. Even the simplest meal of rice and curry with a fried fish on the side feels hearty and fulfilling.

Yes, they offer home delivery and are available on Swiggy and Zomato, which is convenient — but to be honest, the real value comes from dining in. The rising delivery charges and taxes often end up making the same ₹200 meal cost ₹300+. Instead, walk into Nityananda, grab a seat, and enjoy a hot, freshly cooked meal served within minutes. The quick service, buzzing atmosphere, and strong smell of seafood and spices make the experience all the more memorable.

It’s not a fancy place by any means — simple tables, quick-moving staff, a menu that hasn’t changed in years — but it doesn’t need to be. The food speaks for itself. It’s no wonder Nityananda has such a strong base of loyal, repeat customers who keep coming back for comfort food that never fails.

If you’re in Goregaon East and looking for a budget-friendly, full-flavored seafood experience, Nityananda Lunch Home should be at the top of your list. It’s not just a restaurant — it’s a local treasure.

I ordered the paya soup and prawns biryani from here.

The prawns biryani was delicious. The prawns were fresh, well cooked, and had that subtle bite you expect, without being rubbery. The biryani rice was aromatic, well infused with masala, and flavorful throughout, making it a very enjoyable dish overall.

The paya soup was good and comforting. The broth had a light yet hearty body with a noticeable peppery warmth and gentle spice from the masala. That said, I would have preferred a deeper meaty and fatty richness in the broth. The paya piece itself was well cooked, with soft meat and gelatinous fat that almost melted in the mouth.

Overall, it was a very satisfying experience, and I will definitely be exploring more dishes from here.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Sai Veg World is one of those rare places that holds a lot of nostalgia while still continuing to evolve, and that’s exactly what keeps me coming back. I have been visiting this place since its inception, back when this building used to be a post office in the early 2000s. Watching it transform into a popular vegetarian restaurant over the years has been quite a journey.

One thing I genuinely appreciate about Sai Veg World is that the management keeps experimenting with new ideas and concepts. They don’t remain stuck in one format, and you can clearly see the effort to improve and adapt with time. That willingness to try new things is something I really like about this place.

The menu offers plenty of variety, especially when it comes to snacks and quick bites. Whether you’re looking for a light breakfast, evening snacks, or a proper vegetarian meal, there’s always something to choose from. The South Indian dishes are the main attraction here and have never disappointed me. From dosas to idlis and other South Indian snacks, the taste has remained consistently good over the years, making it a reliable spot for a quick and satisfying meal.

It’s also a great place for a quick breakfast or snack stop, especially if you’re in the Goregaon East area. Service is generally efficient, and the place manages to handle regular crowd flow fairly well.

Overall, Sai Veg World continues to be a dependable vegetarian restaurant with a lot of variety, a strong South Indian focus, and a management team that keeps trying to innovate. A solid 4-star experience and a place I’d definitely recommend if you’re looking for good vegetarian food in Goregaon East.

featured_reviews.name: Raj Patil
featured_reviews.review_text:
I ordered the Misal from South Tiffin House through

Zomato after reading a few good reviews, but it turned out to be quite disappointing. The Misal was extremely oily, and the excess oil completely overpowered the flavor of the dish. Instead of getting that nice balance of spice and tang that makes Misal enjoyable, it just tasted greasy and

heavy.

The farsan portion was another letdown. It was very little, almost like they forgot it's supposed to be an essential part of the dish. Without enough farsan, the Misal lost its crunch and texture, which made it feel incomplete. The pav was fine and the packaging was decent, but the main dish itself just didn't deliver.

I had higher expectations from South Tiffin House, especially since they're known for traditional snacks. With a few improvements, this could actually be a good Misal. If they reduce the oil and serve a more generous amount of farsan, the taste would improve a lot. Right now though, I wouldn't recommend ordering it if you're looking for an authentic, well-balanced Misal. I hope they work on this because the potential is definitely there, but the current version just misses the mark.

featured_reviews.review_text:
It’s disheartening to write a negative review about Idli Dosa Fusion, Malad East, especially since I’ve always appreciated their food quality. However, my recent experience was far from satisfactory.

Service and Hygiene Concerns:

Upon ordering a Masala Dosa, Thate Idli, and Filter Coffee, I was surprised to see the Dosa served on a small paper plate, with the masala in a paper cup typically used for tea. Chutney and Sambar were also served in similar paper cups. The staff mentioned that the cutlery washer was unavailable, but this setup was both unexpected and uncomfortable.

The Thate Masala Idli was presented in the same manner. Additionally, I had to request the staff three times to clean the table, and it was only addressed when I insisted that they take the food back if the table wasn’t cleaned.

Filter Coffee Issue:

The Filter Coffee was initially served in an unclean cup with dried coffee stains. When I pointed this out, the staff claimed it was clean until I showed them the stains, after which they provided a paper cup. I had asked to cancel the coffee order, but they refused, stating it couldn’t be returned.

Lack of Management Communication:

When I expressed my desire to share this feedback with the owner, the staff informed me they didn’t have his contact number.

Suggestions for Improvement:

While I value the taste of the food at IDF, such lapses in service and hygiene are unacceptable. I urge the management to:
•	Ensure proper cutlery and serving dishes are available at all times.
•	Maintain cleanliness, especially given the outlet’s proximity to the road, which can lead to dust accumulation on tables.
•	Provide facilities for customers to wash their hands.
•	Train staff to handle customer concerns with honesty and promptness.

Given the presence of competitors nearby, it’s crucial not to lose loyal customers due to avoidable issues. I hope the management takes this feedback seriously and implements necessary changes.
